en.reason: The writer is the workshop making the bag, so ㉠ asks which color the customer would like it made in. Blank ㉡ requests the chosen color by the day before Wednesday’s production start.
en.trap:
㉠ “이미 만드셨나요”: This asks which color the customer has already made the bag in, changing both the maker and the timing.
㉡ “바꾸어 드리겠습니다”: This changes a request for the customer’s choice into a promise by the workshop to change the color.
㉡ “직접 찾으러 오셨나요”: This asks about a past collection visit instead of requesting the chosen color.
en.strategy: Unlike some other practical writing prompts, the writer here is the seller. Separate who makes the bag from who chooses the color, then check the direction of the polite actions in “드리다” and “주시다.”

zh.reason: 写信人是制作布袋的工坊，因此㉠应询问顾客希望用哪种颜色制作。㉡则请求顾客在周三开工的前一天告知所选颜色。
zh.trap:
㉠“이미 만드셨나요”：这变成询问顾客已经用哪种颜色制作了布袋，制作主体和时间都变了。
㉡“바꾸어 드리겠습니다”：这不是请顾客作选择，而变成工坊承诺更换颜色。
㉡“직접 찾으러 오셨나요”：本应请求告知所选颜色，却询问过去是否亲自来取过。
zh.strategy: 与部分其他实用文不同，这里的写信人是卖方。先分清谁制作、谁选颜色，再确认“드리다”和“주시다”所表示的礼貌动作方向。

en.reason: A blank cell can arise for several reasons, so it cannot automatically be treated as zero, meaning no use. Blank ㉠ calls for distinguishing the two states; ㉡ calls for retaining an unverified status until confirmation rather than filling in a guess as fact.
en.trap:
㉠ “같은 값으로 처리해야 한다”: This opposes distinguishing an unverified entry from an actual zero.
㉡ “가장 흔한 숫자로 채워야 한다”: This substitutes a value from other entries without confirming what the blank means.
㉡ “자료 전체를 없애야 한다”: Erasing verified data because some entries are unverified is not the stated principle.
en.strategy: Distinguish the absence of a number from a value of zero. The sentence giving priority to “확인된 사실” over “보기 좋게” indicates the direction of the final blank.

zh.reason: 空白可能由多种原因造成，不能自动等同于表示实际没有使用的0。㉠要求区分这两种状态；㉡要求在确认前保留为未核实状态，而不是把猜测当事实填入。
zh.trap:
㉠“같은 값으로 처리해야 한다”：这与区分未核实状态和实际为0的要求相反。
㉡“가장 흔한 숫자로 채워야 한다”：这没有核实空白的原因，就用其他项目的数值替代。
㉡“자료 전체를 없애야 한다”：因部分项目尚未核实就删除已经确认的数据，不是文中提出的原则。
zh.strategy: 区分没有数字与数值为0。强调“확인된 사실”优先于“보기 좋게”的句子，指出了最后一个空格应表达的方向。

en.reason: Even an identical figure of 45% refers to a proportion within a different age group. The model compares the groups’ different priorities and the shared ranking of proximity, while respecting the limit that actual respondent counts cannot be established without each group’s size.
en.trap:
“두 연령층 모두 조용한 공간을 가장 중요하게 여겼다”: For people aged 40 and above, reading groups rank highest at 45%.
“가까운 거리를 고른 20~30대가 40대 이상보다 반드시 많다”: The shares are 35% and 30%, but the groups’ sizes are unknown, so the larger number of people cannot be determined.
“2025년 전체 이용자의 45%가 독서 모임을 골랐다”: The 45% is within the group aged 40 and above, not among all users.
en.strategy: Treat each column of the table as a separate 100%. Rankings within each group can be compared, but comparing actual numbers of people between groups requires the total size of each group.

zh.trap:
“두 연령층 모두 조용한 공간을 가장 중요하게 여겼다”：40岁及以上组中，读书会以45%排名第一。
“가까운 거리를 고른 20~30대가 40대 이상보다 반드시 많다”：比例分别为35%和30%，但不知道各组规模，无法判断人数多少。
“2025년 전체 이용자의 45%가 독서 모임을 골랐다”：45%是40岁及以上组内的比例，不是全体使用者中的比例。
zh.strategy: 把表格的每一列分别看作100%。可以比较各组内部的排名，但要比较两组实际人数，就需要知道每组的总人数。

en.reason: The model explains how contributing to production can broaden relationships and understanding. It distinguishes the burdens of coordinating roles, fear of mistakes and pressure to participate, then proposes optional roles, access to help and fallback arrangements if someone stops, linking these to respect for both observing and participating.
en.trap:
Arguing only that every visitor should be required to take the same role: This does not respect the choice to observe or differences in the desired level of involvement.
Discussing only participants’ enjoyment and omitting organizers’ burdens: This leaves out one of the two parties in the second question.
Proposing only that people be left to take roles freely without explanation: This gives too few practical operating conditions, such as role boundaries, support and scheduling.
en.strategy: Do not overlook that people who choose not to participate are also users of the event. Make the criteria for dividing roles and the help available if participation becomes difficult concrete.

zh.reason: 示例说明参与制作可以增进关系与理解，并区分角色协调、担心出错、被强迫参与等负担。随后提出可选择的角色、求助渠道，以及中途退出时的替代办法，把运营措施与同时尊重观看和参与联系起来。
zh.trap:
只主张让所有观众强制承担相同角色：未尊重只观看的选择及参与程度的差异。
只写参与者的乐趣，省略运营者的负担：遗漏了第二个问题中的一个主体。
只提议无需说明、自由交给大家去做：缺少角色范围、支持、日程调整等实际运营条件。
zh.strategy: 不要忽略选择不参与的人也是活动使用者。把角色划分标准，以及参与途中遇到困难时的支持具体化，运营方案就会更扎实。
